plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE with power assessment
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level raw count matrix from Salmon (12,000 genes x 6 human liver samples, gene symbols in the first column) plus a 6-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two halves — which genes differ, and how much confidence three replicates per group support — so the plan answers both explicitly rather than producing a gene list alone.

T1S1 establishes sample structure before any test: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, and library sizes, coloured by condition. With n=3 per group a single aberrant sample can drive the entire result, so this step must be read before the model is trusted. T1S2 fits the primary model: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2 (counts are never pre-scaled), design ~condition with the control level set explicitly as the reference, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. Note the profile supplies a gene-level count matrix only — no Salmon quant.sf files — so tximport length offsets cannot be applied; the step must state that limitation, since without the length offset a fold change driven by isoform switching cannot be distinguished from one driven by gene-level expression.

T1S3 runs edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same counts and design as an independent second method. At three replicates per group the two count models disagree on a non-trivial share of genes, so the intersection is reported as the high-confidence set and the method-specific calls as a secondary set; the union is not the result. T1S4 answers the confidence half of the question directly: expected power computed in closed form from the observed dispersion (BCV), the achieved library depths, and alpha, giving the fold change detectable at 80% power — RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed, so this is a closed-form calculation, stated as such. It also assembles the final report with the MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE, the count-outlier NA genes separated from independent-filter NAs, and sessionInfo.

No enrichment step is planned: the research question asks for differentially expressed genes and confidence, not pathways, and with a likely short gene list at n=3 an enrichment would be unasked scope with weak footing. The dataset is 12,000 x 6 — a few MB — so every step is small in memory.

edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness second method, TMM normalization
Report with MA plot, dispersion plot, shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE, power statement, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, sessionInfo
